title: A Tale of Two Transition Disks: ALMA Long-baseline Observations of ISO-Oph 2 Reveal Two Closely Packed Nonaxisymmetric Rings and a ∼2 au Cavity
question: What do 0.02 arcsec (3 au) resolution Band 6 continuum and 12CO data reveal about the disks of the ISO-Oph 2 wide binary, and what do they imply for the origin of the substructure?

data.sensitivity: Continuum rms 3.6e-2 and 2.7e-2 mJy/beam (long-baseline epochs); 2.4e-1 and 3.7e-1 mJy/beam (lower resolution epochs); line rms 26.5, 18.7, 89.5, 53.4 mJy/beam km/s

what.value: M0 spectral type of the primary and its accretion rate

what.value: K-band flux ratio of 0.08 between the two components

evidence.quote: Adopting the BT-Settl models (cite: Allard2012)

recipe.method: ALMA Science Pipeline calibration of all data sets

recipe.goal: image and self-calibrate the 1.3 mm continuum
recipe.method: TCLEAN of the high-resolution continuum spectral windows with manual masks, then two phase-only self-calibration iterations per epoch
key_parameters: Final beam 0.02'' x 0.03'' centred at 225 GHz

recipe.method: Recentre epochs on the secondary disk, apply continuum self-cal solutions, UVCONTSUB, then combine the 0.02'', 0.2'' and 1.1'' datasets and TCLEAN with auto-masking and a uvtaper to make 1.5 km/s cubes
key_parameters: Auto-masking for regions up to 3 x rms, 1.5 km/s channels

recipe.goal: estimate stellar masses of the two components
recipe.method: Use primary M0 spectral type and 2MASS J-K to derive extinction, then BT-Settl models for mass and age of the primary; use the K-band flux ratio to get the secondary's absolute K magnitude, Teff and mass at the same age and extinction
key_parameters: A_K = 0.53 x [(J-K) - (J-K)_O]; result A_K = 1.3 mag, A_V = 14.5 mag
assumptions: Observed J-K colour is photospheric; same age and extinction for both components

recipe.method: Search a grid of PA, i and centre for the most circular deprojected image, apply unsharp masking (Gaussian-smoothed copy subtracted), and extract radial and azimuthal profiles averaged over each ring
key_parameters: PA = 1.0 deg (E of N), i = 36.4 deg, centre from Gaia DR2 corrected for proper motion
assumptions: The most circular deprojection indicates the right geometry; same basic assumptions as Cieza et al. 2019 for the inner disk dust mass limit

recipe.goal: measure the size and cavity of the secondary disk
recipe.method: IMFIT for FWHM size and position; subtract the primary's CLEAN-model visibilities, shift the phase centre to the secondary, deproject the visibilities and read the first null of the real part (Bessel function) to get the cavity radius
key_parameters: i = 10 deg, PA = 122 deg for the secondary disk
Null at 5000 +/- 500 klambda gives R_cav = 2.2 +/- 0.25 au
assumptions: Face-on narrow ring model: real visibility is a zeroth-order Bessel function and the imaginary part is zero

recipe.goal: inspect the 12CO gas kinematics and morphology
recipe.method: Position-velocity diagram, channel map and intensity-weighted mean velocity (moment-1) map of the 12CO cube
key_parameters: Bridge channel map spans 0.25 to 1.75 km/s

score_reason: Project codes and the main imaging choices (tclean, Briggs 0.5, uvtaper, self-cal rounds) are given and the headline numbers are quantitative, but image geometry, self-cal solints, flux calibrators, kernel sizes and the visibility-profile binning are missing, and the paper does not state data availability.
rediscovery_reason: The cited ALMA projects are in the ALMA archive and the cavity radius, ring radii, inclination, PA and mass estimates are numeric with a mostly defined recipe, though a reproducer must pick the missing imaging and self-calibration settings.
